schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The device that owns the HARBOR through which workflows voyage. It keeps the AGGREGATE REGISTER of the fleet (the TRUTH rung — what is in port, what is still at sea, where each boat stands) and OPERATES THE CLEARANCE GATE for a workflow's state-transition — the refusal itself is the TICKET'S, exercised here on its behalf (ruled 2026-08-10, decisions/2026-08-10-the-ticket-owns-the-refusal: 'the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal'). SUPERSEDED WORDING KEPT: this read 'grants CLEARANCE ... (the AUTHORITY rung — owner-gated, delegable through its gate)', which made the harbor the holder of authority over the boats. It does NOT own the boats (each workflow is owned by its intention), does NOT execute (the crew sails under delegated clearance — the harbor never sails), and does NOT own the rules (transition legality is base-class physics). 'Where you go to query open tickets.' Built in rungs: child a (register.py) is the register alone — a compiled index over two vantages already on disk (OPEN boats = tickets voyaging in CairnCommons/tickets/; IN-PORT boats = components with a history.json beside their code); primitives `register()` -> {open, in_port, fleet, counts}; `open_boats(reg)` / `in_port(reg)` / `find(reg, id)`. child b (clearance.py, PROVEN 2026-07-24) is the CLEARANCE gate — `clear(workflow, target, *, actor, boat_id, boat_owner, proven_by, resources=None, grant=None, history_path, state_path)` binds authority (Law 6, owner-gated + delegable per-operation via `mint_grant`/`Grant`, non-ambient), proven-space (Law 8 — `proven_by` is the PROOF'S ADDRESS and the gate asks the seal beside it via `validation_store.standing`; the code is proven, never called), room on the host (the fourth refusal, ratified 2026-08-04 — a verdict pulled from system_rackmount's `ask` door, never a reading), and the wrapped base-class rules+truth (Law 4/7, `base/transitions.emit`) before a cursor moves.
why: A workflow-transition factors into THREE rungs (MAP.md, the emit-chokepoint trichotomy resolved 2026-07-21): RULES (is this transition legal for this class? — base-class physics, inherited, un-delegable), AUTHORITY (who may invoke it? — owner-gated, delegable per-operation, non-ambient, Law 6; and the OWNER whose gate that is belongs to the boat, not to the harbor — see the peer clause in `owner`), and TRUTH (record it — local in each boat's own history, central in this register). This gives the record-and-clearance half of the chokepoint a HOME without becoming the ground_loop-executor goof: decision local, record central, execution never here. The register is compiled inference at FLEET scale (Law 1) — 'what is open' answered from structure, not re-derived by walking every boat by hand — the same move as the per-ticket projector (charter-state-history-split), one scale out. It is an INDEX, never a rival record (Law 7): every entry's standing is read from the boat's own cursor and points back to it; the register invents no truth a boat does not already hold, so it cannot drift from the fleet it describes.
invoke: import: `from cairn.devices.harbor_master import register`. Query the live fleet: `python3 -m cairn.devices.harbor_master.register`. Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/harbor_master/proofs/test_harbor_register.py` (exit 0 = green), or under the tester via `TesterDevice().run_proof(...)`. Dependency-light — pure file reads + the projector's pure core; no db_domain, no network; runs bare.
entry: FRESH design, ordinary mechanism. The design — the harbor that gates movement and keeps the register but never sails, the three-rung factoring of a transition (rules/authority/truth), the register as compiled inference one scale out from the per-ticket projector — is Cairn's, converged with Akien 2026-07-21 (the /sorted that landed the harbor-master metaphor and resolved the emit-chokepoint into a trichotomy). The mechanism is pure file reads + the projector's pure core; nothing crossed as carried code. The register is computed on read, so child a's filed db-vs-git placement edge DISSOLVES — there is no stored second copy to place.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)
filed_edges: (a) THE CLEARANCE GATE (child b) — BUILT + PROVEN 2026-07-24 (clearance.py, proofs/test_clearance.py). Grants/refuses a transition through the owner's gate (authority rung), delegable to an igor per-operation via a non-ambient Grant (Law 6); records the movement through the wrapped chokepoint's journal door (Law 7). The base-class emit-chokepoint it clears against (cairn/tools/base/transitions.py) landed the same session, which unblocked it. THE REGISTRY IS GONE (Akien, 2026-08-05: 'methodregistry is a registry. generally we frown on registries. why do we need one here?'). It had been re-instated from the retired ground_loop driver-executor (cairn 584aa74), which DISPATCHED and so genuinely needed name->callable; the executor role was stripped as a goof and the map came back with its consumer changed — clearance.py discarded the callable it returned. What replaced it: `clear` takes `proven_by`, the proof's own path, and asks `tester/validation_store.standing()` — the seal already lives at a DERIVED address (proofs/x.py -> validations/x.json), so proven-space is a traversal, not a second in-memory copy someone has to populate (Law 6 — the fact attaches at its endpoint). The in-memory/durability edge filed here therefore DISSOLVES: the store was always durable git-JSON. And the gate GAINED the check the cache could not have — every VALIDATION promises 'valid until the proof file or the code it proves changes', and `source_fingerprint` (one sha256 over the component's *.py, recorded by the tester at seal time) is what makes that horizon checkable, so a green seal whose code has moved underneath it is refused (Law 3). STILL FILED: the clearance gate has no runtime FACE / bus-fronting yet (an igor calls `clear` in-process today) — deferred until the rack pulls it.

(b) THE VOYAGE VIEW (child c) — BUILT + PROVEN 2026-07-24 (voyage.py, proofs/test_voyage.py, 4 teeth, sealed under a real netns). The TRAFFIC IMAGE: state-right-now, composed as DATA over the register. Two derived, computed-on-read structures — the EMERGENT GATE (at-sea boats grouped by transition-class; many workflows share one gate) and the VOYAGE STITCH (`_canon` normalises the hyphen/underscore id-spelling so `harbor-master` joins `harbor_master`, the join `find()` left open — filed-edge e now closed for the stitch). The one honest flag today is MID-VOYAGE (a boat at sea AND berthed — the silently-stuck, the boon of the broad view); the rest of the design's marker vocabulary ([R]/[X]/[W]/[F]/starvation) is filed grow-against-need on the gate's-queue IOU (`voyage.GROW_AGAINST_NEED`; design in CairnCommons/notes/held-traffic-image.json). Rendered by web_server child d at /harbor. Owns nothing (a projection over the register, Law 7).

(c) DONE-BUT-NOT-BERTHED is surfaced, not resolved: a ticket at cursor PROVED still living in tickets/ shows as an OPEN boat standing PROVED — migration debt the harbor makes visible (Law 7, honest index). Auto-berthing a PROVED ticket into its component history is a later move, not child a's.

(d) COMPUTED ON READ — no stored register. If fleet queries turn hot, an event-fired cache (the FileChanged pattern the intentions_model_compiler uses) is the grow-against-need step; never a poll. Do not add it before a hot query exists (build-minimal).

(e) ID NORMALIZATION — CLOSED for the stitch (child c): `voyage._canon` normalises hyphen↔underscore so a boat's two vantages join under one voyage. `register.find()` still matches literally (its rung's honest job — show each source faithfully); the join lives in voyage, one layer up.

(g) THE FOURTH REFUSAL — UNRESOURCED. RATIFIED AND BUILT 2026-08-04 (cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py, proven in proofs/test_clearance.py). The gate binds three refusals today (unauthorized/Law 6, unproven/Law 8, illegal/Law 4). Akien: 'it's not asking the system anymore. it's asking the harbormaster, because that's the entity that would hold up the license to advance. and that's fine. we're still in the harbor!' So a build may also be refused for NO ROOM ON THE HOST — the harbor asks system_rackmount 'is there room, by my line?' and gets a VERDICT, never a reading (Law 6 stays intact end to end; see that device's charter, known_consumers.the_access_mode_the_consumers_need). THE GRANT GETS AN EXPIRY: 'the thing asks for it, and has 10 seconds to take it to the build gate.' Grant is already frozen and per-operation (boat, target, actor) — this is one field, and the expiry is what lets the resource owner correct its own lagging instrument (it knows it said yes, and knows when that lapses). NOTHING COUNTS BUILDERS anywhere in this chain — admission is decided from PRESSURE, not population, so the fleet register is never consulted to gate a build and stays display-only ('it doesn't manage, it just reports' — Akien, same session). BEYOND THE GATE, for now: 'once past that, it'd go to you, at least for the foreseeable future. once we have more than one builder we can start specializing' — one builder means no dispatch, no routing, no specialization to build yet, which is what makes this whole proposal a simplification rather than a new subsystem. WHAT SHIPPED: `Unresourced` as the fourth refusal, raised before `emit` is reached so a refused move leaves no partial record like every other refusal; `HARBOR_LINES` as the lines the harbor owns; `resources` injected as anything with `ask(name, value) -> bool`; and on Grant, `issued_at` + `ttl_seconds` (10.0) with `GrantExpired` subclassing Unauthorized. The teeth: a grant that names the right operation and lapsed is refused and writes nothing, while the same grant inside its window still clears (so the expiry refuses the STALE, not the DELEGATED); and the proof's resource owner RAISES on every door but `ask` — on the raw reading and on every census shape — so a build that pulled a number or counted a fleet dies on a path whose happy case is identical. WHAT IS STILL RED: (1) nothing in the running system passes `resources=` yet, so the gate is BUILT AND UNWIRED — the default is no resource check, which is honestly a harbor with no view of the host, not a harbor that decided there was room. Wiring it is the next stone and needs a live system_rackmount instance the harbor can reach. (2) HARBOR_LINES' memory value (1024 MB) is a HYPOTHESIS, labelled as one in the code (Law 3) — nobody has measured what a builder needs to not thrash. The cpu value (75%) is derived from Akien's measured 6-of-8 crawl point and is only as good as that. (3) BOTH LINES ARE MEANT TO BE LEARNED, not set — ruled by Akien 2026-08-05: 'we wanna watch what it costs to spin up another x, and in future be able to yeah/nay based on data, not a number out of akien’s head.' Baseline + marginal cost per builder gives the ceiling by division, and every term is observable. That makes HARBOR_LINES' two numbers explicitly TEMPORARY — placeholders holding the seam open until the measurement runs — and it also exposes an assumption buried in the cpu value: 75.0 encodes 'one builder costs one runnable', which nobody has measured. Akien's worked example of 2026-08-05 — baseline 20%, +10 points per builder, 6 builders reaching 80% with the rest kept as headroom — is CONSISTENT with that assumption (~0.8 runnable per builder on 8 cores), not evidence for it. It also adds a term the line will need: a RESERVE, the headroom the host keeps for itself, which is why the ceiling is (usable − baseline) / marginal and not simply 100 / marginal. The design lives in system_rackmount's charter (how_it_learns, item 3), because the METRIC's owner is where a metric learns; the harbor keeps owning the line, it just stops inventing the number.

(h) A charter's `retired` key is a wall, and the reverse read is blind out loud — BUILT + PROVEN 2026-08-18 (ticket a-superseded-intention-is-never-silent). Three additions, one seam. (1) `clearance.retirement_of` reads an added top-level `retired` key off a charter dict ALREADY IN HAND — measured free: a retired and a living charter both cost exactly 2 file opens, because `boat_owner_of` had already opened the charter to read `gated_by`. The key lives on the SUPERSEDED charter, which INVERTS the prior art at `ruling.supersede` and does so deliberately: a retired ruling packet is SIGNED and may never be touched, so its link must live on the successor; a charter is an authored record that grows by ADDITION, the successor-side read would cost a 56-charter scan per crossing, and a successorless deprecation must be expressible (`superseded_by` is nullable). What DID transfer from that door is the discipline — evidence required, normalise on READ never by rewrite, refuse naming every lack at once. A malformed key raises `RetirementUnreadable` and is NEVER collapsed into 'not retired' (Law 7). (2) `clearance.riders_of` is the REVERSE of `boat_owner_of`: given an intention address, which in-flight boats name it — and it returns, always and even at zero, the three classes it could NOT attribute (no owning_intention; an address resolving under neither root; a state whose flight cannot be judged). A scan reporting only what it found is a green earned by not looking, and the proof carries a mutation tooth that reds if any blind class is dropped — a tooth that caught a real hollow in this build on its first run, when `attributable` was DERIVED and the partition identity therefore stayed true by arithmetic no matter which class was removed. Live at build: 69 in flight, 22 attributable, 40 unattributed, 7 unresolvable, 3 unreadable. (3) Step 1b of `_decide` refuses a FORWARD crossing of a boat whose owning intention is retired, naming the supersession and the successor. A RETREAT IS EXEMPT — a wall, not a gate — because a retreat is how such a boat gets dealt with, and the harbor decides nothing beyond the refusal: ending, re-parenting, or letting it through anyway is the OWNER's act (Law 6), exactly as with every other refusal here. The build added NO TRACING of its own, measured by an ast census: the trace store still has exactly one writer (`_trace_attempt`) called from exactly one place (`clear`), whose frame-level try/except already records every refusal that leaves the function — including ones nobody has thought of yet. READ FACE: `python3 -m cairn.devices.harbor_master.register <intention address>` prints the deprecation report, findings and all three blind counts together. Watched by probes/a_superseded_intention_is_never_silent.py.
gates: proof gate (tester) — a proof a hollow build could not pass: QUERY the fleet and get BOTH open and in-port boats non-empty with their standings (a register that can only show one berth proves nothing about querying the fleet — the non-hollow floor); show the register is an INDEX over the boats' own truths, not a rival record (every in-port standing is byte-equal to project(that boat's history).cursor; every open standing is read from the ticket's own state — drift reds it, Law 7); show every boat points back to a source that exists (the index references, never replaces); show open ∪ in_port is exhaustive and berth-disjoint (no boat invented or lost). Durability gate: proven, persisted beside the proof via validation_store.persist_validation, committed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) the register shows only one berth over the real fleet (open OR in_port empty) — it cannot answer 'query the fleet', the whole point; (2) a register entry's standing diverges from the boat's own record (an invented or stale truth — Law 7 breach, a rival record not an index); (3) a boat's source does not exist on disk (the index points at nothing); (4) a boat appears in neither or is silently dropped (fleet != open ∪ in_port). Wrong-intent signals (the design slips Akien named): if the harbor starts EXECUTING or SCHEDULING work it is the ground_loop-executor goof; if it comes to OWN the boats (mutating a workflow's content, not just indexing its movement) it has become the fleet owner, not the harbor; if devices advance workflows AROUND it once the clearance gate lands (ambient transitions), the authority rung has failed (Law 6).  ||  MEASURED 2026-08-10 — THIS FALSIFIER IS MET, and has been continuously since the gate landed 2026-07-21. Of 186 emit-shaped records across the component histories, ZERO carry cleared_by; grep finds no production caller of clear() anywhere (every call site is in harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py). So 'devices advance workflows AROUND it' is not a risk this charter is watching for — it is the whole recorded life of the system, and the authority rung has failed by this component's own stated test. Akien RULED 2026-08-10 (decisions/2026-08-10-clearance-is-mandatory) that clearance is MANDATORY and emit must refuse a crossing carrying no cleared_by — so the falsifier stands as written and it is the CODE that must move to meet it, not the sentence that must soften. Cast as ticket emit-refuses-an-uncleared-crossing; this component is RED until that door refuses (Law 9).  ||  AND THE CODE MOVED TO MEET IT — 2026-08-10, ticket emit-refuses-an-uncleared-crossing PROVED. The falsifier stands written exactly as it was; what changed is the world. THE SIXTH SEAT: cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit now refuses a forward journaled crossing INTO A REST that carries no cleared_by and names no exemption (ClearanceRequiredRed), and it RE-READS the witness against the world — the named proof must stand in proven-space now, at the seal date the record claims — so a hand-typed cleared_by forges nothing. THE FIRST CLEARED CROSSING IN THE SYSTEM'S RECORDED LIFE is cairn/tools/base/history.json seq 35 — the entry carries its own stamp — and the count moved 0 -> 1 of 192 there. THE CAUSE, which is the part worth keeping: the rung did not go a year uncalled through indiscipline — clear() was structurally UNCALLABLE for every gated crossing from 2026-07-29, because three gates inside emit read journal_extra['ticket'] and clear() accepted no **journal_extra, so a caller doing everything right was refused with TicketRequiredRed. Physics pointed the wrong way and nothing said so because nobody was calling it to find out. WHAT IS STILL RED, and it is this component's own rung: the AUTHORITY refusal is the one of clearance's four that reads only its caller's arguments — actor and boat_owner arrive in the same call, so a caller satisfies the Law 6 check by choosing what it types. Found by the FIRST LIVE FIRE (the first production call raised Unauthorized, and the fix was to type a different string) and cast as ticket boat-owner-is-read-not-stated. So the sentence above — 'if devices advance workflows AROUND it, the authority rung has failed' — is no longer met by BYPASS, and is not yet un-met by ENFORCEMENT: three of the four refusals (proven-space, resources, legality) read from where the caller does not write and are binding on every crossing into a rest; the fourth is a declaration until that ticket lands.
how_it_learns: NOTHING IS BEING HARVESTED, AND AS OF 2026-08-10 THE PRECONDITION IS NOT MET EITHER — this field claimed it was. The old text read 'With clearance gating transitions, each cleared crossing records WHO cleared it ... The precondition is met (an honest, non-drifting record of every cleared move)'. Measured 2026-08-10: zero crossings have ever been cleared, so there is no such record and never has been. The learning surface is OPEN IN CODE (child b landed and is proven) and EMPTY IN THE WORLD. What the design still intends, unchanged: each cleared crossing records who cleared it and whether it was delegated, so the boats' histories become evidence of how the fleet actually moves — which transitions stall, where boats pile up, which clearances get delegated to which igor. That is the raw material for learns-its-gates. What does not exist: any judgement over that evidence — the gate applies fixed rules (owner-or-grant) and does not adjust a clearance policy from what it has seen. Build-minimal still holds — do not build the learner before there is a fleet moving through the gate — but the honest reason it is deferred is now that NO fleet moves through the gate, not that too few do. Unblocked by ticket emit-refuses-an-uncleared-crossing.  ||  THE PRECONDITION IS NOW PARTLY MET — 2026-08-10. The claim above ('zero crossings have ever been cleared, so there is no such record and never has been') was true when written and is now false: 1 of 192 emit-shaped records carries cleared_by, delegated and the proof the clearance leaned on (cairn/tools/base/history.json seq 35). The learning surface has its first row. It stays deferred, and the honest reason changes shape rather than going away: n=1 by one hand cannot tell a gate that works from a gate that agrees with whoever calls it — which is exactly what ticket boat-owner-is-read-not-stated is about — so what would be learned from this evidence today is the caller's habits, not the fleet's. The watch that will say when that stops being true is armed at probes/clearance_actually_gates.py: it clears only when 20 post-era crossings have all cleared or been exempted AND clearance has refused a real one.
traces_to: Law 1 (the aggregate is compiled, not re-derived — fleet-scale compiled inference, the projector one scale out)
Law 7 (the register is a record of truth: an index over the boats' own histories, append-only in each boat, never a rival that drifts)
Law 6 (exactly one owner; the clearance rung is owner-gated, delegated only through the gate — child b)
Law 4 (the rules are base-class physics, not the harbor's to grant — gates, not supervisors)
Law 8 (a cursor moves only onto code in proven-space — the gate reads the tester's own seal beside the proof, and refuses one whose horizon has closed; no registry, no second copy)
build order: harbor_master, after the heartbeat+bus+system-device+inference+web-server block; waits on the charter-split (done) + the base-class emit-chokepoint (child b's dependency) — MAP.md:996
owner: CC owns harbor_master's code + proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the design ratification (the harbor-master metaphor and the three-rung transition factoring, converged 2026-07-21: 'looks good to me') and the node-class definitions. Each boat is owned by its own intention — the harbor indexes the fleet, it does not own the boats.  ||  IT IS A PEER SYSTEM, AND THE AUTHORITY RUNG WAS NEVER THE HARBOR'S — RULED 2026-08-10 (decisions/2026-08-10-the-ticket-owns-the-refusal). Akien: 'the harbormaster owns the harbor. he reports on the state of it. the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal.' / 'it's a peer system' / 'the boat is owned by the ticket... or is the ticket depending on point of view. and the intentions always own their tickets.' / 'and yes, the ticket owns the workflow'. THE CHAIN, end to end: an INTENTION owns its TICKET, a ticket owns its WORKFLOW, and the workflow IS the boat — one object seen from two vantages, which is why `boat_id` has always been the ticket id. So the refusal a crossing meets is the boat's own, and this device operates the gate as its agent. NO DEVICE SITS ABOVE A BOAT. On the superseded wording, in his words: 'i think that authority component was added extremely early in our harbormaster process before we had it all worked out. but everybody is a peer supserceeds that.' — so the AUTHORITY-rung claim in `what` and `why` is early drift, not a design this ruling overturns, and the sentence already standing in this field ('Each boat is owned by its own intention — the harbor indexes the fleet, it does not own the boats') was the conforming half all along. IT WAS ALSO THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION SETTLED WRONG SIX DAYS LATER: `boat_owner` was derived from Law 6 plus the shape of the comparison in clearance.py while this field held the answer verbatim (present since 02d0a5a, 2026-08-04). WHAT IS STILL RED HERE: the code has not moved yet. clearance.py's `boat_owner` paragraph still settles the owner as a MOVER and the gate still reads the value from its caller — ticket boat-owner-is-read-not-stated, whose child (a) ('where a boat carries its owner') this ruling ANSWERS: it is carried by the ticket, under the intention that owns it.
gated_by_why: THE HANDS THIS INTENTION'S OWNER-GATE ADMITS — the machine-readable half of `owner` above, and the only half `cairn.devices.harbor_master.clearance.clear()` reads. Compared by EXACT LIST MEMBERSHIP, never by scanning: an actor is admitted iff it equals a member of this list. WHY A NEW FIELD RATHER THAN READING `owner`: measured 2026-08-10 across the 24 beside-code charters, 22 carry an `owner` longer than 60 characters (this one runs past 2000) and 2 carry an EMPTY one — so matching an actor against that prose is a substring scan, which is a check that goes green for the wrong reason (an actor named 'C' matches nearly everything). The prose says WHO and WHY for a human reader; this list is what a gate can stand on. Law 6's second clause still binds: a hand that is not a member does not become one by naming itself — standing comes through the owner's gate, which here means through a grant minted by a member, or through an edit to this list, which is itself an owner-gated write to this charter. SCOPED TO THIS ONE CHARTER ON PURPOSE (build-minimal, grow against need): every other intention keeps prose until its own first gated crossing needs the field, and until then the gate REFUSES that component's crossing while naming this field, that charter's path, and the one-line fix. Whether that refusal is a kindness or a tax is a claim, not a fact, and it is watched rather than asserted. The fleet-wide fill, and the question of who may MINT on an intention's behalf, are filed as ticket an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands rather than absorbed here. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: nothing here grants standing over any OTHER intention's tickets — a boat's owner is the intention named in its ticket's `owning_intention`, and no device sits above a boat.

Teeth mutation-checked: inverting _under, inventing a harbor line, and pinning ask() to True and to False each turn their tooth red. Runs bare — no bus, no daemon, no instance.
